sections.body: Peer pressure is feeling pushed to do something to fit in. It can be positive (joining a study group) or negative (risky dares, being unkind to someone).
Healthy friends respect your 'no', support you, and don't make you feel bad for being yourself.
CONSENT in everyday life means asking and respecting the answer: before borrowing things, sharing someone's photo, or hugging. Consent can be changed at any time.
Saying no: be clear and short ('No thanks'), suggest something else, or leave. Real friends will accept it.

quiz.q: A friend wants to post a funny photo of you, and you say no. A good friend will…
options: Respect your answer and not post it
hints: If you ask to borrow a pen and they say no, you don't take it anyway.
quiz.explain: A good friend respects your 'no'. That's consent.

quiz.q: Which is an example of POSITIVE peer pressure?
options: Friends encouraging you to join a study group
Friends daring you to skip school
hints: Which choice is good for you?
A teammate encouraging you to practise more is positive. Which option is similar?
quiz.explain: Being encouraged to study together is positive peer pressure.
